EVELYN A. TROMPETA 23 APR 2013 DILG-Region VI 6 Pepita Aquino Street, Fort San Pedro, Iloilo City Dear Dir. Trompeta: This refers to your 18 February 2013 letter which requests the Central Office's official stand through a legal opinion on whether it is correct to recognize Vice Mayor Christopher B. Maguad as the acting mayor of the Municipality of Valderrama, Antique during Mayor Mary Joyce R. Roquero's suspension on the basis of the presumption of regularity of the performance of official functions of the concerned local government unit and its officials and considering further that the issues involved are pending resolution before the COMELEC and other tribunals. Before addressing your concern, may we direct your attention to Section 3 (m), Rule 131, Title IV (Revised Rules on Evidence) of the Revised Rules of Court, to wit: "Section 3. Disputable presumptions. — The follotping presumptions are satisfactory if uncontradicted, but "lay be contradicted and overcojne by other evidence: (Ill) That official duty has been regularly performed;" The disputable presumption of regularity in performance of official duties was explained/ discussed by the Supreme Court in the case People of the Philipines vs. Carlos de Guzman y Panaligan (G.R. No. 106025. Every doubl as to an officer's act being or unlawful, construction should be in [11001" of.its lilt('fulness.' Considering that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan's Decision suspending Mayor Roquero is an official act, the same enjoys the presumption of regularity which may only be overcome by contrary evidence before the regular courts of justice or tribunals and administrative bodies having jurisdiction on the same. Notably, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan's Decision imposing the penalty of four (4) months suspension without pay against Mayor Roquero, which included a violation of Republic Act No. 3019 or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, was received through counsel of Mayor Roquero, Atty. Eduardo Seguera Fortaleza, on 08 February 2013, as certified by Antique Sangguniang Panlalawigan Supervising Administrative Officer Evangeline M. Palcat. As a consequence thereof and so as not to paralyze or impede the operations of the local government of Antique, the Department is duty-bound to recognize Vice Mayor Maguad as acting mayor during Mayor Roquero's suspension (considering that the Decision of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan suspending Mayor Roquero is presumably regular and rendered in good faith), pending resolution of the issues before the COMELEC and other tribunals. In view thereof, the recognition of' Vice Mayor Maguad is proper, unless otherwise declared by competent authority. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary
